additions.name: Sherlock
additions.description: Python CLI that checks whether a given username exists on 400+ social networks by probing per-site URL patterns and response signatures.

additions.name: WhatsMyName
additions.description: Free browser-based username checker built on a community-maintained JSON dataset covering 600-700+ sites, with CSV export and no signup required.

additions.name: Maigret
additions.description: Sherlock-derived Python OSINT tool that checks 3,000+ sites for a username and extracts secondary identifiers (bio, email, links) from matched profile pages.

additions.name: GHunt
additions.description: Open-source Python tool that queries Google account internals from an email address to recover a linked profile name, photo, and public Google-service activity.

additions.name: Holehe
additions.description: Python CLI that checks 120-300+ sites for whether an email is registered by exploiting password-reset-form response differences, without notifying the target.
additions.notes: Multiple 2026 community reports say the project has been largely unmaintained since 2022 and a majority of site checkers are now broken; verify hit rate before relying on it and consider Maigret/OSINT Industries as supplements.

additions.name: Hunter.io
additions.description: Commercial email-finder and verifier that locates and validates corporate email addresses tied to a domain or person; free tier gives 25 searches/25 verifications monthly.
additions.notes: Does not cover personal webmail (Gmail/Outlook); only corporate-domain addresses.

additions.name: Epieos
additions.description: OSINT platform that takes an email or phone number and returns linked Google account data and hits across 100-560+ platforms depending on the access tier.
additions.notes: Free tier is limited; the 560+-platform 'LEA/Private' tier is restricted to vetted government/law-enforcement/professional-investigator accounts.

additions.name: OSINT Industries
additions.description: Commercial real-time checker that takes an email, phone number, or username and returns linked accounts across 200+ platforms for investigators and law enforcement.

additions.name: Have I Been Pwned
additions.description: Free breach-notification search: enter an email or domain to see which of 1,035+ known breaches (17.8B+ records) it appeared in; paid API v3 adds programmatic/bulk lookup.

additions.name: DeHashed
additions.description: Paid breach-search engine returning full compromised records (email, username, IP, and password fields) collected from clear-web and deep-web leak sources.
additions.notes: Grey area: results can include plaintext or hashed passwords tied to a real identity. Included only because it is widely cited in mainstream security press (Krebs on Security, BleepingComputer) as a legitimate investigator/law-enforcement tool, not a credential-stuffing shop. No free tier as of 2026.

additions.name: Intelligence X
additions.description: Search engine and permanent archive indexing breach records, paste sites, dark-web/.onion content, historical WHOIS, and leaked documents by email, domain, or other selectors.
additions.notes: Grey area: full breach records can include plaintext/hashed passwords. Included because it is a long-running (est. 2018), mainstream-press-cited (Wired, TechCrunch) European company, not a criminal marketplace. Free tier capped at 10 results/search.

additions.name: SpiderFoot
additions.description: Open-source OSINT automation framework with 200+ modules that pivots across a domain, email, IP, or person to build a correlated reconnaissance report via web UI or CLI.

additions.name: Recon-ng
additions.description: Modular Python reconnaissance framework, pre-installed on Kali Linux, with a marketplace of modules integrating sources like Shodan, Hunter.io, and HIBP for person/domain OSINT.

additions.name: Maltego
additions.description: Commercial link-analysis platform mapping entities and relationships via 'transforms'; its browser-based Maltego Search checks 200+ social platforms and breach data by email/username.

additions.name: theHarvester
additions.description: Open-source OSINT tool that gathers emails, subdomains, names, and IPs tied to a domain or organization from search engines, certificate-transparency logs, and other public sources.

additions.name: PhoneInfoga
additions.description: Open-source CLI that scans an international phone number for carrier, line type, and country data and generates search-engine footprint links for further pivoting.

additions.name: NumLookup
additions.description: Free international reverse phone lookup returning carrier, geographic region, and line type (mobile/landline/VoIP); does not disclose subscriber identity.

additions.name: Spokeo
additions.description: Commercial people-search aggregator combining property, court, business, and social-network records (billions of records) for name, phone, and address lookups.

additions.name: UserSearch
additions.description: Commercial OSINT investigation platform offering 17 search types (username, email, phone, image, crypto, vehicle, court records) with case management for investigators.

additions.name: Indicia
additions.description: Pay-per-credit OSINT platform aggregating 39+ sources and 600B+ records for US person lookup, breach data, reverse face search, and 40+ platform username search.

additions.name: Fingerprint
additions.description: Public-data search engine checking a username, email, or phone across 700+ platforms in parallel and recursively surfacing linked accounts; free demo without account.

additions.name: CourtListener / RECAP
additions.description: Free Law Project's nonprofit search engine for US federal court opinions and PACER dockets (via the crowd-sourced RECAP archive), searchable by party name or case keyword.

changes.name: Pipl
changes.detail: Pipl eliminated its free/self-signup people-search tier and moved to enterprise-only custom pricing (roughly $3,000-$130,000/year), making it no longer viable for individual OSINT practitioners.

changes.name: PeekYou
changes.detail: The PeekYou people-search aggregator's domain no longer resolves; confirmed offline as of July 2026.
